transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Um… yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because there’s been this situation with my ensemble work that I haven’t really been able to get past.

It’s not like I want to make a big dramatic thing out of it, but for almost two years now I’ve felt pretty certain that after a commission I did, a few people in the ensemble started sort of… quietly working against me. Like with schedule changes, where people sat, little comments during rehearsals—things that sound small, I know. And they’ve shown me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but it still feels like those explanations don’t really cover what’s happening.

I’m not sure if that’s the right way to say it. I just haven’t been able to shake it, and it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Do you believe for certain that these ensemble members are intentionally working against you?

I mean… “certain” sounds strong, and I don’t want to seem unreasonable. But yes, honestly, I’ve had a hard time believing it’s accidental.

After that commission, it really started to feel like a few of them were using things like schedule changes, where people were seated, and these small comments in rehearsals to kind of quietly undermine what I was doing. They’ve shown me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, and I try to take that in, but it just… doesn’t fully account for what I’m seeing. So yes, I guess I do feel pretty sure about it.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or energized?

I don’t think so… I mean, I can get excited when a project is going well, or kind of keyed up before a rehearsal, but I wouldn’t say it’s unusually high or anything like that.

At least, not that I’ve noticed. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m replaying a rehearsal or someone’s comment in my head, but not like hearing an actual voice when nobody’s there.

I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean.
If someone showed you clear proof that your coworkers were not trying to undermine you, would you be able to accept that?

I’d like to say yes, because I don’t want to seem like I’m just refusing to listen. If it was really clear proof, I would try to take it seriously.

But… honestly, that’s been part of the problem. They have shown me emails or notes that are supposed to explain the schedule changes or seating decisions, and I can understand what they’re saying on paper, but it still doesn’t fully settle it for me. It’s like it doesn’t explain the timing, or the little comments in rehearsal, or the pattern of it after that commission.

So I guess… I’d want to be able to accept it, and I’d try. I’m just not sure I could shake the feeling completely. Is that okay to say?
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Not most of the day, nearly every day, no. I mean, I have low days, and I can get discouraged, especially when things feel tense, but I wouldn’t say I’m depressed all the time or anything like that.

At least… I don’t think so. If there’s a more specific way you mean it, I can try to answer better.
Have other people ever told you that your speech or thoughts seemed disorganized or hard to follow?

No, not that I can remember. I mean, people might ask me to clarify something if I’m talking too fast or getting into details, especially with music or scheduling, but I don’t think anyone has said my thoughts were disorganized or hard to follow.

If anything, I probably over-explain sometimes. Does that count, or do you mean something more extreme?
Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about your coworkers intentionally trying to undermine you?

I mean… I know I’m supposed to say yes, because of course anyone can be mistaken. And I don’t want to sound unreasonable.

But if I’m being honest, it doesn’t feel like just a misunderstanding to me. For almost two years now, since that commission, I haven’t been able to shake the sense that a few people in the ensemble started doing things—schedule changes, seating choices, little comments during rehearsal—that were meant to quietly undercut my work.

They’ve shown me emails and notes that are supposed to explain it, and I can see how, on the surface, those explanations make sense. I’m not trying to ignore that. It just… it still doesn’t fully account for the pattern, at least not to me.

So yes, I guess it’s possible I’m mistaken. I just don’t really feel convinced that I am. Does that make sense?
Aside from the tension with your ensemble, has this situation caused major problems in the rest of your life?

I don’t think so, not major problems. I mean, it’s stressful, obviously, but outside of the ensemble situation I’m still functioning pretty normally.

I meet my deadlines, I’m keeping up with composing, I run most mornings, and things at home with my wife are basically steady. So… I wouldn’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. It’s mostly centered around that one area, if that answers the question.
Have you had a strong sense that ordinary things—like remarks, looks, or events—were actually sending a special message meant specifically for you?

A little, yes… though I don’t know if I’d call it a “special message” exactly.

It’s more like, after that commission, certain ordinary things started to feel pointed—like a schedule change, or where someone seated people, or a comment during rehearsal that could sound innocent but felt aimed at me, or at my work. I know that probably sounds like I’m reading too much into it, and people have shown me emails or notes that explain why something happened.

I can understand the explanations on paper. I just… I haven’t been able to shake the feeling that some of it was meant to quietly undermine me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you lost interest or motivation in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I still care about composing and music, and I still do the things I normally do.

There are days where I’m distracted or not as eager to deal with people, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in things I enjoy. At least, I haven’t noticed anything like that in a big way. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed yourself becoming emotionally flat or less able to express feelings than you used to?

No, I don’t think so. I mean… I’m probably a little more guarded lately, just because I’m watching how I come across, but I wouldn’t say I feel emotionally flat.

My wife would probably tell you I still react to things, still get excited or frustrated or whatever. I don’t think I’ve lost that. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you felt that other people could somehow know your thoughts, even when you did not say them out loud?

No… I don’t think it’s that exactly. I haven’t felt like people can literally hear my thoughts or know what I’m thinking without me saying it.

It’s more that I’ve had this certainty I can’t shake that, after the commission, a few people in the ensemble were using ordinary things—schedule changes, seating decisions, small comments in rehearsals—to sort of quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, I can understand that, but it still feels… intentional.

But not like they know my thoughts. Does that make sense?
Do you believe these coworkers have any impossible or supernatural way of influencing you, or is it only through ordinary actions like emails, seating, and comments?

No, not supernatural. I don’t think they have some impossible way of affecting me or anything like that.

It’s more… ordinary things. Emails, rehearsal comments, where people get seated, schedule changes—things that could look normal, I guess. But after the commission, I just haven’t been able to shake the feeling that a few of them were using those things to quietly push against my work.

I know that probably sounds strong. And when they show me explanations, like emails or notes, I can see what they’re saying. I just… it still feels intentional to me. Does that make sense?
Outside of this issue with the ensemble, have you become socially withdrawn from other people?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ve probably been a little more careful around the ensemble, but outside of that I’m still functioning pretty normally, I think.

I’m still meeting deadlines, keeping up with composing, running most mornings… and things at home with my wife are basically steady. So I wouldn’t say I’ve withdrawn from people in general. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had busy stretches where I stayed up too late working on music, but I wouldn’t say I needed less sleep and felt unusually energized or anything like that.

If I don’t sleep enough, I’m usually tired the next day, like anyone else. Is that what you mean?
Before this problem with the ensemble began, did you generally tend to distrust other people’s motives?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve always tried to be thoughtful about people’s intentions, especially in professional settings, but I wouldn’t say I generally distrusted people before this.

At least, not in a way that caused problems. I’ve had normal doubts here and there, like anyone, but nothing that I would have described as a pattern. Does that answer what you’re asking?
